 // TEST[s/^/PUT _data_stream\/logs-nginx.access-prod\nPUT _data_stream\/logs-my_app-default\n/]
 // end::alias-multiple-actions-example[]
 
+[discrete]
+[[Multiple action results]]
+=== Multiple action results
+
+When using multiple actions, if some succeed and some fail, a list of per-action results will be returned.
+
+// tag::alias-multiple-actions-result-example[]
+Consider a similar action list to the previous example, but now with an alias `log-non-existing`, which does not yet exist.
+In this case, the `remove` action will fail, but the `add` action will succeed.
+The response will contain the list `action_results`, with a result for every requested action.
+
+[source,console]
+----
+POST _aliases
+{
+  "actions": [
+    {
+      "remove": {
+        "index": "index1",
+        "alias": "logs-non-existing"
+      }
+    },
+    {
+      "add": {
+        "index": "index2",
+        "alias": "logs-non-existing"
+      }
+    }
+  ]
+}
+----
+// TEST[s/^/PUT \/index1\nPUT \/index2\n/]
+
+The API returns the following result:
+
+[source,console-result]
+--------------------------------------------------
+{
+  "acknowledged": true,
+  "errors": true,
+  "action_results": [
+    {
+      "action": "remove",
+      "success": false,
+      "error": "aliases_not_found_exception"
+    },
+    {
+      "action": "add",
+      "success": true
+    }
+  ]
+}
+--------------------------------------------------
+
+Allowing the action list to succeed partially may not provide the desired result.
+It may be more appropriate to use set `must_exist` to `true`, which will cause the entire action
+list to fail if a single action fails.
+
+// end::alias-multiple-actions-example[]
+
 [discrete]

generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The change from `AcknowledgedResponse` to `IndicesAliasesResponse` in multiple files is consistent. However, ensure that `IndicesAliasesResponse` provides all necessary information and functionality that was previously available with `AcknowledgedResponse`. Specifically, check if methods like `.isAcknowledged()` are still applicable and correctly implemented.

In `AliasAction.java`, the exception message in `throw new AliasesNotFoundException(alias);` should be consistent with the previous message for clarity. Consider using a similar format: `"required alias [" + alias + "] does not exist"` or updating all instances to use the new message style.

The `must_exist` parameter description in `docs/reference/indices/aliases.asciidoc` is inconsistent with the behavior described in other files. The doc states that `must_exist` affects the behavior when attempting to remove an alias which does not exist, but it should also clarify its effect on the entire action list. In contrast, the code and tests imply that `must_exist` only affects the specific removal action.

review_comment: I am a little uncomfortable with the change made in this file. Specifically, the use of the actionResult variable which is modified throughout the main loop over actions. Also, the fact the the action result is added to the final actionResults list at different places in the code. This is done because of the use of `continue`  in a few places. I think a better design would require a refactor of this loop to remove the use of `continue` statements. I was trying to avoid changing the code too much ... but kinda seems like I already passed that point.
We can leave the refactor as a follow-up, if you want to open an issue for it. I agree that it'd be nicer to write it in more of a functional style.
